system_description.narrative_title: Global bond selloff, rising yields and central‑bank repricing
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is a worldwide repricing of interest‑rate expectations: rising inflation (partly driven by higher oil/energy prices and geopolitical shocks) has pushed long‑term sovereign yields to multi‑decade highs, provoking hawkish signals from central bankers and ad‑hoc market interventions. Seen as an open system, flows of information, commodity shocks, policy signaling, investor positioning and fiscal constraints interact in feedback loops that amplify volatility across bonds, currencies, equities and government borrowing costs. The interaction produces oscillating phases of panic, policy response and temporary calm as new information (oil moves, Jackson Hole speeches, interventions) crosses the system boundary and drives re‑adaptation.
system_description.scope: Global sovereign bond markets and connected transmission channels: long‑term yields and curves, inflation expectations, central bank policy communications and decisions (Fed, ECB, BOJ, Bank of Canada), oil/energy prices, investor flows and interventions (hedge funds, bond funds, Treasury operations), major currencies and equity market spillovers; primary focus on US, Eurozone, Japan, UK and Canada.
adjacent_subsystems: Sovereign fiscal policy and public debt sustainability

variables.name: Long-term nominal yield
variables.description: Representative market level of long-duration nominal government bond yields.

variables.name: Short-rate expectation
variables.description: Market-implied expected trajectory of short-term policy interest rates.

variables.name: Realized inflation rate
variables.description: Measured change in the general price level (e.g., CPI/PCE) over a recent period.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: Medium- to long-term expected inflation embedded in surveys and markets.

variables.name: Commodity and energy price level
variables.description: Aggregate market price level for key commodities, with emphasis on energy.

variables.name: Term structure slope
variables.description: Difference between long-term and short-term yields indicating curve steepness.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: Component of long-term yields reflecting compensation demanded for duration and uncertainty.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: Ease and depth of executing large fixed-income transactions without large price impact.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: Degree of short-term price variability in bond and closely linked markets.

variables.name: Investor positioning
variables.description: Aggregate directional exposures, hedges and risk allocations across bond market participants.

variables.name: Net capital flows to bonds
variables.description: Net periodic inflows or outflows into investment vehicles holding fixed-income assets.

variables.name: Policy communication tone
variables.description: Overall hawkishness, clarity and intensity of monetary and fiscal policy messaging as perceived by markets.

variables.name: Aggregate fiscal borrowing needs
variables.description: System-wide public sector financing requirement over a specified horizon, expressed relative to economic size.

variables.name: Market intervention activity
variables.description: Frequency, scale and targeting of ad-hoc operations aimed at influencing asset prices or yields.

variables.name: Fixed-income leverage
variables.description: Average leverage ratio across participants and vehicles exposed to bond markets.

variables.name: Credit risk premium
variables.description: Average yield spread demanded for credit risk relative to benchmark risk-free rates across debt markets.

catalysts.title: Federal Reserve September policy decision
catalysts.description: FOMC decision (raise or hold) will reprice short‑rate expectations and reshape the yield curve; markets expect a decisive signal this month.
catalysts.rationale: Markets debate whether Fed will raise or hold after Warsh and Waller comments ("Warsh ... raise if inflation doesn't ease"; "Waller ... support holding rates steady").

catalysts.title: ECB upcoming policy decision
catalysts.description: Euro‑area central bank meeting likely to signal further rate hikes amid rising inflation, prompting euro‑area yield repricing.
catalysts.rationale: Eurozone inflation rose above 3%, cementing ECB rate‑hike bets ("Euro zone inflation rises above 3%, cementing ECB rate hike bets"; "ECB must be prepared to lift interest rates further").

catalysts.title: Sustained energy and oil price rise
catalysts.description: Ongoing upward pressure in oil and gas prices will feed through to inflation readings and bond yields if sustained.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines link rising oil/energy to bond selloffs and inflation worries ("Oil Prices Push Global Bond Market Closer to the Edge"; "Energy price surge hits bond markets").

catalysts.title: Escalation in Middle East tensions
catalysts.description: Further geopolitical escalation would raise energy risk premia and safe‑asset term premia, boosting global yields and volatility.
catalysts.rationale: Reports tie Middle East turmoil to revived inflation fears and higher long yields ("Long‑Term Treasury Yields Rise as Iran War Revives Inflation Worries"; "Middle East turmoil reignites inflation fears").

catalysts.title: Bank of Japan possible September tightening
catalysts.description: BOJ signals a chance of a September rate move; any tightening would propagate yen repricing and affect global yield curves.
catalysts.rationale: BOJ chief signaled a chance of a September hike, pushing yen and global bonds ("BOJ chief signals chance of September rate hike"; "Yen jumps ... bet on Japan interest rate rises").

catalysts.title: U.S. Treasury yield‑cap operations / interventions
catalysts.description: Ongoing or expanded Treasury interventions to cap long yields could directly compress term premia and alter market liquidity/positioning.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines detail Treasury moves and private interventions to cap long yields ("Treasury Raises the Stakes in a Battle to Cap Long‑Term Yields"; "Bessent ... bond intervention").

catalysts.title: Higher fiscal borrowing costs and issuance pressure
catalysts.description: Rising yields increase debt servicing costs and may force larger issuance or fiscal adjustments, adding supply pressure to bond markets.
catalysts.rationale: Articles warn rising yields add tens of billions to G7 debt costs and threaten developing country debt ("Rising bond yields add tens of billions to G7 countries’ debt costs"; "IMF's Georgieva says rising bond yields threaten progress on developing country debt").

catalysts.title: Net flows into/out of bond funds and portfolio shifts
catalysts.description: Continued retail and institutional bond fund flows — and tech issuance in euro markets — will alter demand/supply balance and investor positioning.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note investors still pouring money into bond funds despite selloff and shifting demand in euro bond market ("Rising yields aren’t scaring off investors. Why money is still pouring into bond funds."; "US tech firms may crowd out others in euro bond market").

catalysts.title: U.S. November midterm elections
catalysts.description: Midterms will shape fiscal and regulatory outlooks, affecting policy tone and longer‑term yield premia as political uncertainty grows.
catalysts.rationale: Commentary links Fed, politics and markets ahead of midterms, suggesting elections will influence policy and yield dynamics ("Warsh puts Fed on collision course with Trump ahead of midterms").
